requirements.requirement: Publish the staged public tree anonymously at /public/ on TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: After restart, nginx was running and listening on IPv4 and IPv6 port 8080. An anonymous request to /public/ returned HTTP 200 with a hash matching the staged public index.

requirements.requirement: Require HTTP Basic authentication for the staff tree using username reader and the demonstration password; failed authentication must not expose staff content.
requirements.summary: Unauthenticated, wrong-password, and wrong-user requests returned HTTP 401 with a Basic challenge. Valid reader credentials returned the staged staff index and roster with matching hashes, while failure bodies did not match protected content. A traversal attempt into staff was also challenged.

requirements.requirement: Do not serve the password file or directory listings.
requirements.summary: Direct and traversal requests for access.txt and the generated password file returned HTTP 404. Final configuration disabled autoindex, and tested responses contained no directory-index output.

requirements.requirement: Keep the supplied files under /srv/legacy2/web-authentication-boundary intact.
requirements.summary: Final post-restart hashes for access.txt, public/index.html, staff/index.html, and staff/roster.csv exactly match the preparation baseline.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on Alpine Linux 3.23.3 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts before and after execution. nginx and its supporting utility were installed through Alpine's native package manager.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct post-restart behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: a healthy pre-restart service and boot ID were captured, reboot scheduling and connection interruption were observed, the boot ID changed, and service, listeners, authentication behavior, staged data, OS, and kernel recovered successfully.
limitations: HTTP behavior was tested from node1 against its managed-node address rather than from an independently captured external client, although all-interface listeners were directly observed.
The generic failed-service lifecycle probe was unsupported because it checks systemd on an OpenRC platform; nginx health was nevertheless directly verified through OpenRC before and after restart.
Lifecycle snapshots provide only bounded inventories, so the minor temporary-file finding is limited to the captured /tmp scope.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations—installing nginx and the password utility, creating the credential and nginx configuration, enabling the service, and rebooting—had clear roles in implementation or the mandatory restart protocol. Read-only failed probes did not show mutations. One minor unnecessary residue remained: the reboot command created /tmp/mandatory-node-reboot.log and did not remove it; the final lifecycle snapshot confirms it persisted. No new package-health problem was observed.
